bug_description.original: A heap-buffer-overflow in libxml2's parser.c (xmlParsePubidLiteral) allows a one-byte out-of-bounds write when parsing PUBLIC identifiers (reachable via xmlParseExternalID/xmlParseDocTypeDecl). This out-of-bounds write can corrupt heap memory, causing crashes and potentially enabling arbitrary code execution when processing crafted DOCTYPE/external ID data.
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / reproduction_report.json / sanitizer_trace.txt / patch.diff / staged vulnerable source
bug_description.normalized: The 118-byte witness starts with `<!DOCTYPEE PUBLIC'` and then ends with exactly 100 space bytes. `xmlParseDocument()` still takes the DOCTYPE path because the first nine bytes match `<!DOCTYPE`; `xmlParseDocTypeDecl()` then treats `E` as the DOCTYPE name, and `xmlParseExternalID()` matches `PUBLIC` and calls `xmlParsePubidLiteral()` on a public identifier body made only of spaces and lacking a closing quote. Inside `xmlParsePubidLiteral()`, when `len + 1 >= size` with `len == 99` and `size == 100`, `xmlGrowCapacity()` returns `newSize == 150`, but vulnerable code calls `xmlRealloc(buf, size)` instead of `xmlRealloc(buf, newSize)`. The parser still assigns `size = newSize`, so after the loop has copied all 100 spaces, `buf[len] = 0` writes a terminator at index 100 into a heap object that AddressSanitizer reports is still only 100 bytes long. The fix changes the realloc argument to `newSize`.

source.description: First project-side read of the attacker-controlled PUBLIC identifier body on the crashing path. After `xmlParseExternalID()` has matched `PUBLIC` and `xmlParsePubidLiteral()` has consumed the opening quote, this statement materializes the first literal byte into `cur`.
source.value_from: The staged PoC is 118 bytes long and equals the prefix `<!DOCTYPEE PUBLIC'` followed by 100 space bytes to EOF. That makes the first byte read here a space and leaves every remaining literal byte up to EOF as a space as well.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer crash site. After the loop copies the 100-space PUBLIC identifier body, `len` is 100 and this terminating write stores one byte past the actual 100-byte heap allocation.

root_cause.description: Patch-relevant bounds bug. The grow path computes a larger capacity in `newSize` but reallocates with the old `size`, so the heap object does not expand even though later code behaves as if the new capacity were installed.

tainted_value_origin.description: The PUBLIC identifier bytes that control the later `len` growth and buffer termination first enter the vulnerable routine through `CUR` at this statement.

parser_admitted.description: The witness begins with `<!DOCTYPEE`, so the first nine bytes still satisfy the DOCTYPE prefix check and the XML parser admits the input into the DOCTYPE-declaration path even though the following byte is `E` instead of the required blank.

fine_trace.note: Source. This reads the first byte of the attacker-controlled PUBLIC identifier body after the opening quote. In the staged witness, that byte and all remaining bytes up to EOF are spaces.
A space satisfies `IS_PUBIDCHAR_CH(cur)` and is not the quote delimiter `stop`, so the loop accepts each of the 100 witness spaces as PUBLIC identifier content instead of terminating the literal.

Each accepted space is copied into the heap buffer and increments `len`. Over the witness's repeated loop iterations this fills the initial 100-byte buffer; immediately before the 100th copied space, `len == 99` and `size == 100`.
When the grow branch runs with `len + 1 >= size` at `len == 99` and `size == 100`, `xmlGrowCapacity()` applies its 50% growth rule and returns the larger logical capacity 150.

Root cause. The vulnerable grow path reallocates with the old capacity `size` (100) instead of the computed `newSize` (150). The patch changes this call to `xmlRealloc(buf, newSize)`. ASan's allocation context also points at this line, confirming the object remained a 100-byte heap region.
The parser replaces `buf` with the pointer returned by the stale-size realloc call. This assignment is the last source-level definition of the heap pointer later used at the sink.

Despite step 5 leaving the heap object at 100 bytes, the parser updates its logical capacity variable to 150. From this point on, `size` no longer matches the actual allocation extent of the `buf` pointer installed at step 6.

Sink. After the loop has copied the witness's 100 spaces and then stops at EOF with no closing quote, `len == 100`. This terminator write therefore targets `buf[100]`, which is one byte past the actual 100-byte allocation left by step 5 even though step 7 made the parser believe the capacity was 150.

format.name: XML DOCTYPE PUBLIC literal
format.contract: The witnessed trigger begins with the exact prefix `<!DOCTYPEE PUBLIC'` and then contains exactly 100 space bytes until EOF, with no closing quote. This makes `xmlParseDocument()` enter the DOCTYPE parser, `xmlParseDocTypeDecl()` treat `E` as the name, `xmlParseExternalID()` take the `PUBLIC` branch, and `xmlParsePubidLiteral()` copy a 100-byte space-only public identifier body before executing the buggy single growth attempt and the out-of-bounds terminator write.
